note: Classic transitive past-tense agent+theme clause skeleton, confirmed by three near-synonymous examples (buy/purchase/acquire).
Same recurring past-tense transitive skeleton as AgThPast but with an affected Patient (repair/fix/mend a gearbox).
Ditransitive agent-transfers-theme-to-recipient is a standard recurring frame (give/teach/lend), despite 'the query' being an odd Recipient.
Bare tense-neutral transitive agent+theme core (permit/forbid/allow) is a standard minimal clause frame.
All three examples clearly also have a Theme (photography), so bundling only Agent+Location and dropping the obligatory Theme looks like an arbitrary partial slice, not a natural standalone unit.
Tense-neutral transitive agent-patient causative core (repair/cancel/call off) is the same recurring family as AgPatPast minus tense.
Genuine locative/existential predication where Location is the core predicate complement (X is located at Y), not a dropped adjunct.
Agentless patient-undergoes-change-in-past (unaccusative/passive) is a real recurring frame; the third example's by-phrase agent is a minor wrinkle since passive agents are canonically omissible.
Theme+Location as a stative locative/inclusion core is plausible in principle, but two of three examples are too garbled to confirm the pattern.
Minimal event+central-theme pairing (what the event is fundamentally about, agent-agnostic) is a plausible recurring unit, especially for non-agentive subjects like 'a recipe needs eggs.'
Minimal intransitive agent-only frame (walk/stroll/arrive); the dropped goal/time phrases are genuine optional adjuncts, not missing core roles.
Minimal unaccusative patient-only frame (survey begins/starts/commences); the dropped time adjunct ('at dawn') is optional, not core.
Discover's real core is Agent+Patient, both obligatory and both dropped in favor of the peripheral Location alone; example 2 ('An error discovers an auditor') is also semantically nonsensical.
